Board 03 — U2, the audit journal viewer GET /api/v1/journal · portfolixir.journal.list

U2 — the audit journal viewer, the two-way coverage debt standing since Sprint 19: GET /api/v1/journal and portfolixir.journal.list exist, no screen does. Q5 — A, one page „Audit-Journal“ (/journal), newest first, filtered by actor, operation and kind, each row linking to its entity and to that entity's own history. B, a „Verlauf“ fold on each entity's page, is drawn for contrast. „Q5 B“ flips it. Q6 — the entry sits in the sidebar's „Verwaltung“ group, after „Klassifizierungen“; „Q6 tab“ moves it to a third Transactions tab.

dashed = new or changed · amber edge = a synthetic row written into the shipped markup of a real one (the seed has no such row) · 1 ties a change to its section's text. Synthetic data only.

A — one page, the API's shape /journal · Verwaltung → Audit-Journal

The seed's journal, filtered to the agent: the seven writes of the API token „review seed“ (actor api_token_rw), read from audit_journal, newest first. The seed wrote them within one second, so they share a time.

  • 1Q6: the low-traffic „Verwaltung“ group, where the other record-keeping pages are (ADR-0022's five areas). There is no Settings page to hang it from.
  • A Transactions tab would say the journal is about bookings; it holds every entity kind.

1Columns map JSON.journal_entry/1: inserted_at (UTC, as the history's since note), actor_type with its actor_label (the token's name) as the second line, operation, resource_type + resource_id as the entry with its current name, and the change. 2Filters are the API's: actor and operation as chips, the kind as a select, include_scenarios as a checkbox; the basis line restates them. 3„Gespeicherte Werte“ folds the stored before/after to the changed fields; the line above says the change in words. A delete shows its stored values with „—“ after.

Per-entity links: the entry links to its page where it has one (a rule to Risiko, an account to Konten & Depots, a tax statement to Steuern); „Nur dieser Eintrag“ filters by resource_type + resource_id, so one entity's history is a URL. A deleted entity has no page and reads as text.

Q5, recommended A. (1) The operator's question is global: „what did the agent change this week?“ crosses entity kinds, and only one list answers it. (2) It matches the API's shape, one list with the same filters, so a link an agent hands over can open the same slice. (3) One surface, built once. B needs a fold on every page that shows an entity (securities, accounts, depots, views, rules, targets, tax statements, categories), and a booking has no page of its own, so B cannot show the most frequent entry at all. A gives B's per-entity view through „Nur dieser Eintrag“.

B on Meridian Global Equity ETF: its two journal entries (the ISIN change of the Sprint 16 merge and its creation). It answers „what happened to this security“ where it is read, but no question across entities, and nothing for a booking.

Found while drawing. (1) S3, idea: the API has no time filter, so „this week“ is read by paging newest-first; a since= on /api/v1/journal, mirrored on the page as on the history, would answer it directly; it needs its own story (API and MCP first). (2) S3: a booking has no URL of its own, so the journal (and any agent hand-over) can link a transaction only to the history as a whole. (3) S3, to check against the API reference: a delete entry's after repeats the deleted record instead of being empty, so a reader comparing before/after sees no change; the page reads the operation, not the diff.
